## Proof

Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional inner product space over \(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\) with inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V\), and let \(L(V,V)\) be the space of linear operators on \(V\). For \(T\in L(V,V)\), let \(T^*\) denote its adjoint with respect to \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V\).

**Construction.** Define the *Hilbert–Schmidt* inner product on \(L(V,V)\) by
\[
\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle \;:=\; \operatorname{tr}(S^*T), \qquad S,T\in L(V,V),
\]
where the trace is taken with respect to any orthonormal basis of \(V\).

**It is an inner product.** Let \(\{e_1,\dots,e_n\}\) be an orthonormal basis of \(V\).

*Hermitian symmetry:*
\[
\langle\!\langle T,S\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(T^*S)=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((S^*T)^*\big)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle}.
\]

*Linearity in the second argument:* \(\langle\!\langle S,\alpha T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(S^*\alpha T)=\alpha\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)=\alpha\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle\).

*Positive definiteness:*
\[
\langle\!\langle T,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(T^*T)=\sum_{i=1}^n\langle T^*T\,e_i,e_i\rangle_V=\sum_{i=1}^n\langle Te_i,Te_i\rangle_V=\sum_{i=1}^n\|Te_i\|_V^2\ge 0,
\]
with equality iff \(Te_i=0\) for all \(i\), i.e. iff \(T=0\).

Hence \(\langle\!\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\!\rangle\) is a genuine inner product on \(L(V,V)\).

**The map \(*\) is self-adjoint.** The adjoint operation satisfies the involution property \((S^*)^*=S\) and the trace is cyclic, \(\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)\). Using these,

\[
\langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((S^*)^*T\big)=\operatorname{tr}(ST).
\]

We must show this equals \(\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle\) (when \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\), so \(*\) is linear) or its conjugate \(\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle}=\langle\!\langle T^*,S\rangle\!\rangle\) (when \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\), so \(*\) is conjugate-linear). In both cases the right-hand side is

\[
\operatorname{tr}(S^*T^*)=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((TS)^*\big)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(TS)}=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}.
\]

- **Real case (\(*\) linear):** \(\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\operatorname{tr}(ST)\), so
  \[
  \langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle,
  \]
  which is exactly self-adjointness of the linear operator \(*\).

- **Complex case (\(*\) conjugate-linear):** a conjugate-linear operator \(A\) is self-adjoint iff \(\langle\!\langle AS,T\rangle\!\rangle=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,AT\rangle\!\rangle}\) for all \(S,T\). With \(A=*\),
  \[
  \langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle},
  \]
  so \(*\) is self-adjoint as a conjugate-linear operator.

**Basis-free summary of the key identity.** The entire argument rests on two facts: the involution \((S^*)^*=S\) and cyclicity of the trace. Together they give
\[
\boxed{\;\langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle}\;}
\]
over \(\mathbb{R}\) (dropping the conjugation) and over \(\mathbb{C}\) respectively, which is precisely the self-adjointness of \(*:T\mapsto T^*\) with respect to the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product \(\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)\).

## Proof

Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional inner product space over \(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\) with inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V\), and let \(L(V,V)\) be the space of linear operators on \(V\). For \(T\in L(V,V)\), let \(T^*\) denote its adjoint with respect to \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V\).

**Construction.** Define the *Hilbert–Schmidt* inner product on \(L(V,V)\) by
\[
\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle \;:=\; \operatorname{tr}(S^*T), \qquad S,T\in L(V,V),
\]
where the trace is taken with respect to any orthonormal basis of \(V\).

**It is an inner product.** Let \(\{e_1,\dots,e_n\}\) be an orthonormal basis of \(V\).

*Hermitian symmetry:*
\[
\langle\!\langle T,S\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(T^*S)=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((S^*T)^*\big)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle}.
\]

*Linearity in the second argument:* \(\langle\!\langle S,\alpha T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(S^*\alpha T)=\alpha\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)=\alpha\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle\).

*Positive definiteness:*
\[
\langle\!\langle T,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(T^*T)=\sum_{i=1}^n\langle T^*T\,e_i,e_i\rangle_V=\sum_{i=1}^n\langle Te_i,Te_i\rangle_V=\sum_{i=1}^n\|Te_i\|_V^2\ge 0,
\]
with equality iff \(Te_i=0\) for all \(i\), i.e. iff \(T=0\).

Hence \(\langle\!\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\!\rangle\) is a genuine inner product on \(L(V,V)\).

**The map \(*\) is self-adjoint.** The adjoint operation satisfies the involution property \((S^*)^*=S\) and the trace is cyclic, \(\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)\). Using these,

\[
\langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((S^*)^*T\big)=\operatorname{tr}(ST).
\]

We must show this equals \(\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle\) (when \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\), so \(*\) is linear) or its conjugate \(\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle}=\langle\!\langle T^*,S\rangle\!\rangle\) (when \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\), so \(*\) is conjugate-linear). In both cases the right-hand side is

\[
\operatorname{tr}(S^*T^*)=\operatorname{tr}\!\big((TS)^*\big)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(TS)}=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}.
\]

- **Real case (\(*\) linear):** \(\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\operatorname{tr}(ST)\), so
  \[
  \langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle,
  \]
  which is exactly self-adjointness of the linear operator \(*\).

- **Complex case (\(*\) conjugate-linear):** a conjugate-linear operator \(A\) is self-adjoint iff \(\langle\!\langle AS,T\rangle\!\rangle=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,AT\rangle\!\rangle}\) for all \(S,T\). With \(A=*\),
  \[
  \langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle},
  \]
  so \(*\) is self-adjoint as a conjugate-linear operator.

**Basis-free summary of the key identity.** The entire argument rests on two facts: the involution \((S^*)^*=S\) and cyclicity of the trace. Together they give
\[
\boxed{\;\langle\!\langle S^*,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(ST)}=\overline{\langle\!\langle S,T^*\rangle\!\rangle}\;}
\]
over \(\mathbb{R}\) (dropping the conjugation) and over \(\mathbb{C}\) respectively, which is precisely the self-adjointness of \(*:T\mapsto T^*\) with respect to the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product \(\langle\!\langle S,T\rangle\!\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(S^*T)\).
